edges.rationale: Credit and demand conditions shape what firms decide.
A recession moves results of every firm.
Past conditions are already in the balance sheet.
Weak firms cut staff, cash-rich firms buy: decisions follow the state.
Growth and margins persist and revert by themselves.
Managers act on what they expect and outsiders cannot see.
What they expect tends to happen, with or without the decision.
The same state triggers several decisions at once.
A merger and a layoff in one year cannot be told apart by their results.
Most decisions change costs or capacity first.
Products and reach change what customers buy.
Costs reach margins with a lag.
Demand reaches revenue with a lag.

omitted: Accounting choices around a decision, such as restructuring charges.
Effects on other firms: a rival's layoff or merger is not independent of this one.

rules: Audit: no effect is estimated until the event registry audit says credible.
Sample: at least 30 usable events for matched, weighted and event-study designs.
Support: at least 90% of treated firms inside the controls' propensity range.
Balance: every standardized mean difference at most 0.25 after matching.
Pre-trends: at most one lead per outcome with its 95% interval away from zero.
Placebo dates: at most one in ten away from zero.
Null: at most 10% of pseudo-event draws rejected at a nominal 5%.
Synthetic control: half of the events usable, holdout error at most 1.5 times the fit.

treatments.estimand: Average effect of a yearly change of R&D expense on growth and margins 4 to 7 quarters after it was reported, against matched firms without such a change.
assumptions: Conditional parallel trends: without the action, treated firms would have moved like their matched controls.
No anticipation before the first public document.
Overlap: firms like the treated also exist without the action.
One version of the treatment: the same label means the same action.
No interference between firms.
Effects of R&D may take longer than any window here.
untested: Management expectations are not measured: pre-trends can look fine and still be driven by a plan outsiders cannot see.
Parallel trends after the event can never be tested, only made plausible before it.
No interference between firms is assumed, not checked.
